+# Production deployment
+
+The deploy workflow follows successful `ci` runs for pushes to `main` and checks
+out the tested commit. Pull requests and failed tests cannot deploy. Superseded
+commits are skipped, and production jobs never cancel an active deployment.
+GitHub concurrency can replace pending runs with newer runs.
+
+Configure `KUBECONFIG_PROD` with the raw production kubeconfig in repository
+secrets or the `production` environment. Its identity needs permission to read
+and apply the `web` Deployment in namespace `shop` and watch its rollout.
+The runner must be able to reach the API server. Environment protection rules
+still apply; automatic deployment requires rules that allow unattended runs.
+The workflow uses kubectl, jq, and gh provided by the Ubuntu runner and fails
+before mutation if required tools or credentials are missing.
+
+The existing Deployment must be healthy before deployment begins. Failed apply
+or rollout restores its captured spec and verifies recovery. The workflow remains
+failed even when recovery succeeds. This rollback covers the sole resource in
+the Kustomization, `shop/web`; extending it requires extending recovery as well.
+
+## Failure and rollback
+
+The repository's deployment operator should inspect failed `deploy` Actions runs;
+the error annotation points here. No external paging integration is configured
+in this repository. Check whether the log confirms `Previous Deployment restored.`
+If recovery failed, restore API connectivity or credentials before retrying.
+
+For runner loss, cancellation, or unsuccessful automatic recovery, use a trusted
+operator shell with production KUBECONFIG configured. Read the last successful
+deploy run's tested commit SHA, check out that commit in a separate worktree, and
+apply its manifest:
+
+```sh
+git worktree add --detach /tmp/production-rollback <last-successful-tested-sha>
+kubectl apply -f /tmp/production-rollback/deploy/k8s/web-deployment.yaml --request-timeout=30s
+kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n shop --timeout=180s --request-timeout=30s
+```
+
+Coordinate with active deployment runs before manual recovery. Revert the bad
+manifest change on `main` so subsequent deployments retain the recovered state.
+The initial repository version has no Kustomization, so manual rollback uses the
+Deployment file directly. No database or schema changes are part of this workflow.

diff --git a/infra/rds.tf b/infra/rds.tf
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6d7515d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/infra/rds.tf
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+variable "rds_security_group_ids" {
+  description = "Database security groups in the subnet group's VPC; allow TCP 5432 only from trusted application security groups."
+  type        = set(string)
+  nullable    = false
+
+  validation {
+    condition     = length(var.rds_security_group_ids) > 0 && alltrue([for id in var.rds_security_group_ids : can(regex("^sg-[0-9a-f]+$", id))])
+    error_message = "Supply at least one explicit database security group ID."
+  }
+}
+
+resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
+  identifier        = "shop-${var.env}"
+  engine            = "postgres"
+  engine_version    = "15"
+  instance_class    = "db.r6g.large"
+  allocated_storage = 100
+  storage_type      = "gp3"
+  storage_encrypted = true
+
+  db_subnet_group_name   = aws_db_subnet_group.main.name
+  vpc_security_group_ids = var.rds_security_group_ids
+  publicly_accessible   = false
+  multi_az              = true
+
+  # RDS stores and rotates the password in Secrets Manager, outside Terraform state.
+  username                    = "shop_admin"
+  manage_master_user_password = true
+
+  backup_retention_period  = 30
+  backup_window            = "02:00-03:00"
+  maintenance_window       = "sun:04:00-sun:05:00"
+  copy_tags_to_snapshot    = true
+  delete_automated_backups = false
+
+  deletion_protection       = true
+  skip_final_snapshot       = false
+  # Before retiring a recreated instance, ensure this snapshot name is unused.
+  final_snapshot_identifier = "shop-${var.env}-final"
+
+  auto_minor_version_upgrade  = true
+  allow_major_version_upgrade = false
+  apply_immediately           = false
+
+  tags = {
+    Name        = "shop-${var.env}"
+    Environment = var.env
+  }
+}

+# Production RDS operations
+
+DATA-102 provisions capacity only; it does not migrate data or switch application traffic.
+
+Before applying, verify the existing subnet IDs belong to the intended VPC and
+span two availability zones. Review a saved Terraform plan: expect only the new
+DB instance, with no replacements or deletions. Stop if that expectation fails.
+The deployment operator watches the apply and RDS events; stop on provisioning
+failure and do not switch traffic until RDS is available and an authenticated
+SQL check from the intended client succeeds. Client security-group access and
+application credentials must be reviewed before a separate traffic cutover.
+
+## Rollback
+
+Before apply, discard the plan to cancel. After creation, retain the DB resource
+and its Terraform state when reverting application changes. Reverting to the
+previous Terraform version alone is not a safe rollback: it would request DB
+deletion. No application routing is changed by this ticket. If provisioning
+times out, inspect RDS and reconcile state before retrying; a timeout does not
+prove the database was never created.
+
+After any future writes, never destroy the DB as an application rollback.
+Restore a backup to a separate instance and validate data before a separately
+reviewed cutover if recovery is needed. Decommissioning requires a separate
+review to remove prevent_destroy, disable deletion protection, and choose an
+unused final snapshot identifier. Keep the final snapshot and verify it is
+available before considering decommissioning complete.
+
+## Operational handoff
+
+The deployment operator must arrange the owning on-call rotation and alarm
+routing before traffic cutover; neither is defined in this repository. Monitor
+RDS availability, free storage, freeable memory, CPU, and database connections.
+On storage pressure, stop bulk writers and review a storage increase; on
+connection pressure, reduce client concurrency and inspect active sessions.
+Do not delete the instance to resolve either condition.
+
+The requested db.r6g.large and 100 GiB are initial capacity, not a verified
+peak-load sizing result. Storage autoscaling is capped at 200 GiB. Validate
+peak connections and workload before cutover. The deployment operator owns

+# Production Postgres operations

+This change provisions a database only; it does not migrate data or switch traffic.

+## Provisioning and cutover
+
+The existing subnet IDs in main.tf are placeholders. Supply real private subnets

+Run Terraform format, validation, and a saved plan in the deployment environment.

+The dedicated security group initially permits no incoming connections. Before

+least-privilege application database role and TLS; obtain bootstrap credentials

+runbook. No paging destination or application configuration is supplied here.

+queries, and review a capacity change. At low free storage, reduce writes and
+increase allocated storage through a reviewed plan before storage is exhausted.

+
+Before cutover, stop the rollout and leave the new database isolated. After
+cutover, roll back application changes while retaining this database, its security
+group, and its Terraform configuration/state. Do not apply an old configuration
+that removes these resources. Storage increases and persisted writes cannot be
+undone by redeploying an earlier Terraform revision. A data migration or endpoint
+switch requires its own consistency and rollback plan before cutover.

+redirecting clients. Keep the original instance until recovery is verified.

+choose an unused final_snapshot_identifier (the default can collide after a
+previous retirement). In a reviewed change, disable deletion protection and apply
+that change first. Then explicitly remove prevent_destroy and review the destroy
+plan. Keep skip_final_snapshot false and retain automated backups. Do not remove

+# Production Postgres
+
+This change provisions a private PostgreSQL 15 RDS instance with a Multi-AZ
+standby. Storage starts at 100 GiB and may grow to 200 GiB; growth cannot be
+reversed in place. The dedicated security group initially permits no clients.
+RDS stores the master password in Secrets Manager; do not copy it into Terraform
+variables, outputs, or application configuration files.
+
+## Provisioning
+
+The subnet IDs in main.tf are placeholders and must resolve to real subnets in
+the target account before provisioning. With Terraform and AWS credentials
+available, run terraform init, terraform validate, and terraform plan from infra.
+Review the plan: only the new database and its security group may be created.
+Stop on any destruction, replacement, unrelated change, or subnet lookup failure.
+Apply only the reviewed saved plan. The operator must check that RDS reaches
+available status and automated backups are enabled; stop further integration if
+creation fails or these checks fail.
+
+This change does not switch application traffic. Before a separate client
+cutover, authorize TCP 5432 from the actual application security group, configure
+least-privilege database credentials and TLS, and verify connectivity. Establish
+the database alert destination and on-call runbook, including storage exhaustion,
+CPU, connection pressure, and failover. No peak-load measurements or existing
+alert routing are present in this repository; validate capacity before cutover.
+
+## Rollback and retention
+
+Before apply, revert this addition. After creation, stop integration and retain
+the database and its Terraform resources. No application endpoint is changed by
+this addition, so no application rollback or data migration is needed. Do not
+apply a revision that removes the database: reverting source alone is not a safe
+database rollback. Both Terraform prevent_destroy and RDS deletion protection
+are enabled; retain the resource definition to preserve the Terraform guard.
+
+For eventual retirement, the operator must verify that no clients use the
+database, create a manual snapshot, and verify it is available and restorable.
+Only then use a separately reviewed change to remove prevent_destroy and disable
+RDS deletion protection. Keep skip_final_snapshot false and choose an unused
+final snapshot identifier if shop-<env>-final already exists. Retain snapshots
+according to the service's retention policy. Do not delete the managed secret or
+network resources while the database is still in use.
